faq: Which tools do you use to sync stock?

Where possible the platform's own marketplace connector, such as Shopify's Marketplace Connect or WooCommerce plugins. For more complex cases we use paid sync apps like Linnworks or Sellbrite. You pay the app plan directly.
It depends on the tool and the marketplace. Many updates arrive within a few minutes, while some run on a schedule of 15 to 60 minutes. We test the real delay and tell you what to expect.
What if my SKUs do not match?
That is the most common problem. We clean and match SKUs first, using a sheet that you can approve. Products without a SKU get one added in your store, so each item has only one identity.
Does the sync also create new listings?
No. This service keeps stock and, optionally, prices in step on existing listings. New listings are created through the Listing Creation or Multi-channel Setup services.

desc:
Inventory sync between your store and marketplaces keeps stock counts matched, so a sale in one place lowers the available quantity everywhere else. Ecom Swift LLC connects your store to each marketplace, maps your SKUs and tests the flow with real orders.

## What is inventory sync?

Inventory sync is a connection that shares one stock number across your online store and your marketplace listings. When an item sells on Amazon, eBay or your own site, the connection updates the quantity on the other channels. The link usually runs through an integration app or the marketplace's own connector, and it matches products by SKU.

Without it, someone has to update every channel by hand after each sale. That works for a handful of products and fails quickly as the catalog grows.

## What goes wrong without it

The common failure is overselling. Two people buy the last unit on different channels within the same hour, and one order cannot be filled. You cancel, apologize and take a mark against your seller metrics.

The opposite problem is just as costly. A product shows as out of stock on a marketplace while you have plenty in the warehouse, and the sales go to a competitor. Manual updates are slow, and every copy-and-paste step is a chance to type a wrong number.

## How sync affects your results

Reliable stock numbers protect the part of your account that marketplaces watch most closely: cancellation and fulfillment performance. Fewer cancelled orders means fewer warnings and fewer unhappy buyers. It also saves hours each week that you can spend on sourcing and listings.

Safety buffers add another layer. For a fast seller, holding back a few units from each channel absorbs the delay between a sale and the update. We do not promise a particular sales outcome. The benefit is fewer errors and less manual work.

## What a good sync setup includes

- Every product matched by a unique SKU across the store and each marketplace.
- Stock updates in both directions, so the source of truth is clear.
- Safety buffers for products that sell quickly.
- Alerts for low stock and for mismatches between channels.
- Rules for bundles and multipacks, so a pack of three reduces three single units.
- Per-channel limits where you want to reserve stock for one place.
- Optional price sync, chosen product by product.
- A daily full check that catches anything the live updates missed.
- A written map showing how each product is matched.

## How we set it up

We start by auditing your SKUs. Duplicates, blanks and mismatched codes are the main cause of failed syncs, so we list them and agree on the fixes with you. Then we connect your store and the marketplace through a suitable integration, match the products and set the direction of updates.

We test with a live order on each channel and watch the stock change. The Basic package links one store to one marketplace. Standard adds buffers, alerts, optional price sync and a daily check. Premium links several channels to one stock source, with bundle rules, a sync log review and a short guide for your team. Any app subscription is paid by you directly to its maker.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Give every product one unique SKU and use it everywhere.
- Decide which system holds the true stock count.
- Set a small buffer on products that sell fast.
- Check the alerts when they arrive instead of ignoring them.
- Run a physical stock count before the first sync.

**Avoid:**
- Editing stock by hand in two places while the sync is active.
- Reusing a SKU for different products.
- Syncing every product before you test a small group.
- Letting a supplier feed overwrite your stock without a rule.
- Turning off alerts because they seem noisy.

## Who it is for

A store owner selling the same products on their own site and one marketplace, who has already cancelled an order because stock ran out. A seller adding a second or third channel who wants stock handled before volume grows. A team with a warehouse that ships for several channels and needs one clear count.

## What we need from you

Send a product list with SKUs, tell us which channels you sell on and name the integration tool if you already use one. We need collaborator or staff access to your store and a seller user with limited permissions on each marketplace. We never need your passwords.
